task_title: Spot the concurrency race in session-token attribution
output:
(1) Race: concurrent set-diff session attribution (TOCTOU on a shared session store).

(2) A and B both snapshot `before`, then each create a session. When A reads `after`, `new_ids` can contain B’s session too. `max(new_ids)` (or `max(after)`) may pick B’s id, so A is charged B’s tokens (e.g. 19k vs 200). Same the other way; empty `new_ids` makes the fallback even worse.

(3) Fix: stop inferring by global diff. Have `run_cli` return the created `sess_id` (or a unique run/correlation id written into that session), and export that id only—or isolate stores per worker, or lock the whole before→run→after path.

judgeDetail.rationale: Correctly names the non-atomic before/after diff, explains how A's after set captures B's session so max() mis-attributes, and gives a genuinely race-removing fix (return sess_id/correlation id or lock the path), though it doesn't explicitly note same-prompt content indistinguishability.
